_comment: Model tiers for the dispatcher agent. CONFIG, NOT CODE: swapping a model is a settings change plus a container restart, never an edit to the calling code.

Part 10 turned routing ON: `activeTier` is null, so each turn runs on the tier the router chose. Set it back to "standard" to pin everything to one model again — that is the rollback, and it needs no code change.

The router picks fast or standard ONLY. Reasoning is reached by escalation, never by classification: at this deployment's measured median of ~18,000 input tokens a turn, Opus costs 5x Sonnet, so one reasoning route erases the saving from seven fast routes. Measured on the 69-query reference set, letting the classifier reach for reasoning made routing 43% MORE expensive than the flat Sonnet baseline it was meant to beat.

`id` is the Bedrock inference-profile id actually invoked. Use eu.* only: global.* profiles route outside the EU. Any id can be overridden per tier with BEDROCK_MODEL_<TIER> (e.g. BEDROCK_MODEL_STANDARD).

Availability (verified 2026-09-23, account 039066033404, eu-north-1): Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 are account-gated by AWS. `id` names the model this build TARGETS; `fallbackId` is proven to work in this account today and is used when the primary is unavailable.

2026-11-02: the AWS account that carried Bedrock is gone. `provider` is "anthropic": each tier's `anthropic` block names the same model it targeted on Bedrock, on the Anthropic API (the router moves from Amazon Nova, which the Anthropic API does not offer, to Claude Haiku 4.5). Override per tier with ANTHROPIC_MODEL_<TIER>; MODEL_PROVIDER=bedrock goes back. Embeddings and rerank have no Anthropic equivalent: see docs/move-to-anthropic-api.md.

2026-11-03: every tier on the newest model in its family, confirmed against the Models API with the production key (it serves claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5). Fallbacks are the previous generation, used only when the primary is unavailable. `request` holds the model's own request fields (thinking, effort): the router and fast tier run Haiku 5.5 with thinking off (as Haiku 4.5 ran); Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 cannot turn thinking off, so their effort is set and maxTokens has room for thinking. See docs/move-to-anthropic-api.md › Model generation.

2026-11-03: effort is set for the best answer, not the price (the user's rule: at ~350 turns a quarter the difference is cents). Standard medium (low graded the same on a simple question; medium keeps room for harder ones), reasoning high, extraction medium. Cost per turn is measured by scripts/prod-checks/agent-turn-cost.mjs; the runaway ceiling, not the tariff, is what guards the bill.

standard.purpose: The default for everything in Part 1.

extraction.purpose: Vision: reading AIP PDF pages and charts.

rerank.purpose: Not available in eu-north-1; see docs/aws-bedrock-setup.md.

pricing._comment: USD per million tokens, Anthropic API list prices (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, read 2026-11-03); used for the Settings usage card and the per-turn cost. Matched by substring of the model id, FIRST match wins, so the newer ids come first. Haiku 5.5 is listed at its price for prompts up to 100,000 tokens (over that it is 5x); Bedrock/Nova rows stay for MODEL_PROVIDER=bedrock.
